rationale: The workflow already implements the evidence-supported P-LIT-GHA-CACHE optimization: both the test and playground jobs cache Cargo dependencies (registry, git db, bin, target) via actions/cache@v4 with keys derived from Cargo.lock, matching the dependency-cache pattern demonstrated in the measured experiments. Other candidate patterns are not supported for this workflow: P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is contraindicated because the playground job performs a production Netlify deployment on push to main (release/deployment work); P-LIT-FAIL-FAST and P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST require a matrix strategy, which this workflow lacks; P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW, P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER, and P-LIT-SELECT would reduce required test coverage; P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT and P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT lack representative duration evidence; Bazel, environment-cache, distributed-cache, and tracing-based patterns do not match the Rust/Cargo toolchain or infrastructure scope.
